text: {"claims": [{"id": "c1", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S0", "rel": "entails", "sub": "In PostgreSQL versions before 9.4, freezing was implemented by actually replacing a row's insertion XID with FrozenTransactionId, which was visible in the row's xmin system column"}, {"sid": "P0.S2", "rel": "entails", "sub": "rows with xmin equal to FrozenTransactionId (2)"}], "check": {"kind": "version", "left": "9.3", "op": "<", "right": "9.4"}, "reasoning": "9.3 is before 9.4, so frozen rows carry FrozenTransactionId in xmin, and S2 identifies that as 2."}, {"id": "c3", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S1", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "preserving the row's original xmin for possible forensic use"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "The passage gives the purpose as preserving xmin for forensic use, not reducing WAL volume; the flag-bit part alone does not entail the claim."}, {"id": "c5", "evidence": [{"sid": "P0.S2", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "may still be found in databases pg_upgrade'd from pre-9.4 versions"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "The passage explicitly says such rows may still be found after pg_upgrade, contradicting 'never'."}, {"id": "c12", "evidence": [{"sid": "P6.S1", "rel": "entails", "sub": "if the storage occupied by multixacts members exceeds about 10GB, aggressive vacuum scans will occur more often for all tables"}], "check": {"kind": "arith", "expr": "20 / 2", "op": "==", "value": "10"}, "reasoning": "S1 states the 10GB threshold triggers more frequent aggressive scans."}, {"id": "c13", "evidence": [{"sid": "P7.S0", "rel": "refutes", "sub": "MXID exhaustion will only block a subset of write transactions"}], "check": null, "reasoning": "MXID exhaustion blocks only a subset, not all write transactions."}]}
